title: Quasi-excellent rings are Nagata
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative quasi-excellent ring [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Then $R$ is a Nagata ring [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring].

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary finite type $R$-algebra $S$ which is an integral domain. By [def-exc-excellent-ring], $R$ is Noetherian and a G-ring. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-g-ring] to this finite type map: $S$ is a G-ring, and hence is Noetherian by [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. We shall prove that this arbitrary $S$ is N-1.

source.place: Tag 07QV, lemma-quasi-excellent-nagata, reduction to finite type domains; Tag 07PV, proposition-finite-type-over-G-ring

proof.text: By the J-2 clause of [def-exc-excellent-ring], the regular locus U in Spec S is open. The localization at the zero prime is the fraction field by [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and hence regular local by [lem-weil-pbc-field-regular-ring]. Thus the zero prime belongs to U. The basic opens D(f) form a basis for the spectrum topology [def-weil-affine-spectrum]; choose D(f) containing the zero prime and contained in U. Membership of the zero prime says exactly f ≠ 0. In Lean use PrimeSpectrum.isBasis_basic_opens.exists_subset_of_mem_open, avoiding an explicit closed-complement ideal.

source.place: Tag 07QV, lemma-quasi-excellent-nagata, application of J-2 before the local reduction

proof.text: Put B = S_f using [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. It is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. The spectrum image formula [lem-weil-pbc-localization-spectrum-embedding] puts the contraction p of every prime Q of B in D(f), hence in U. The localization-of-localization identification [lem-weil-pbc-localization-of-localization], implemented by Mathlib IsLocalization.localizationLocalizationAtPrimeIsoLocalization, gives S_p ≃ B_Q. Transport regular localness along this equivalence. This makes B a regular ring by the ring clause of [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-regular-ring-normal] to obtain exactly the local-domain and integral-closedness hypotheses of the local N-1 criterion.

source.place: Tag 0333, lemma-characterize-N-1, normal-principal-open hypothesis; elementary fraction identification of the local rings

proof.text:
For an arbitrary maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $S$, put $A=S_{\mathfrak m}$ and $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak mA$. This is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$ by [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. It is a domain: a zero product $(a/u)(b/v)=0$ gives $wab=0$ for some $w

e0$. Thus $A$ is reduced. Since $S$ is a G-ring, [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] gives that the canonical $\mathfrak n$-adic completion map $A	o\widehat A$ is regular. The target $\widehat A$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian], with ideal $\mathfrak n$. Apply [lem-exc-regular-map-reduced-target] to this specific regular map: $\widehat A$ is reduced.

source.place: Tag 07QV, lemma-quasi-excellent-nagata, reduced local completion; Tag 07QK, lemma-reduced-goes-up

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-analytically-unramified-n1] to $A=S_{\mathfrak m}$: step 4 supplied a Noetherian local integral domain and reduced completion at its own maximal ideal. The conclusion is that $S_{\mathfrak m}$ is N-1. This holds for every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $S$.

source.place: Tag 032Y, lemma-analytically-unramified-easy, part (5), as used in Tag 07QV

proof.text: Now use [lem-weil-pbc-n1-local-characterization] with the Noetherian domain $S$ from step 1, the nonzero $f$ with normal $S_f$ from steps 2–3, and the N-1 property of every maximal localization from step 5. Its conclusion says that the integral closure of $S$ in its fraction field is finite over $S$, that is, $S$ is N-1. Since the finite type domain algebra $S$ in step 1 was arbitrary, every finite type domain algebra over $R$ is N-1.

source.place: Tag 0333, lemma-characterize-N-1, implication (2) to (1), in the reduction of Tag 07QV

proof.text: Apply [lem-exc-universally-japanese-n1-criterion] to $R$ using the universal conclusion of step 6. It follows that $R$ is universally Japanese, i.e. every finite type domain algebra over $R$ is N-2.

source.place: Tag 0351, lemma-check-universally-japanese, as invoked in Tag 07QV

proof.text: For every prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ of $R$, the quotient $R/\mathfrak p$ is a domain and the quotient map is of finite type: every element is a coefficient from $R$, so no algebra generators are needed in [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Apply the universally Japanese property of step 7, interpreted by [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring], to conclude that every $R/\mathfrak p$ is N-2. Together with the Noetherianity of $R$ in [def-exc-excellent-ring], these are exactly the two clauses defining a Nagata ring in [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring].

tool_uses.why: G-ring stability under finite type algebras is a general commutative-algebra input; the Kummer unit does not supply it.
Noetherianity of principal and prime localizations is a general ring-theoretic tool, not a cohomological step of the unit.
Regular Noetherian rings are normal; this is the generic normality input to the local N-1 criterion.
Noetherianity of the local completion is needed before reducedness can ascend along its regular map.
Finite normalization of a Noetherian local domain with reduced completion is the generic local finiteness tool used in the Stacks proof.
The normal-principal-open plus maximal-local N-1 criterion is the exact generic globalization tool; it supplies no Kummer calculation.
